You are making a surgical, additive edit to ONE Python file for an SMS booking gateway. BOUNDARY: write only inside your task directory. You own exactly two output files: ./bland_gateway.py and ./report.md. Do NOT touch any other file, do NOT git commit, do NOT run the gateway, do NOT call any network/API/MCP, do NOT load skills.

STEP 1. Copy /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mott-date-arch/impl-src/bland_gateway.py to ./bland_gateway.py. It is a 2116-line file. You will change exactly ONE function (resolve_relative_date) plus add ONE module-level flag. Every other byte stays identical.

THE GOAL. Today the resolver only accepts clean date phrases and returns None for anything carrying an English ordinal suffix, so "july 28th" returns None. That caused a real patient to be offered the wrong date. Add a legacy-first ordinal fallback, OFF by default, that strips an ordinal suffix from a day number and re-resolves through the existing grammar. It must be structurally impossible for this to change any phrase the resolver already handles, because you only edit the FINAL return None (reached only after every existing branch has already failed).

EDIT 1 - add the flag. There is a helper def _env_bool(name, default) near line 141 and a line CONSUMER_ACCEPT_LEGACY = _env_bool("ECP_CONSUMER_ACCEPT_LEGACY", True) near line 158. Right after that line, add exactly:
    _DATE_ORDINAL_FALLBACK = _env_bool("ECP_DATE_ORDINAL_FALLBACK", False)
Use that exact env name, that exact constant name, default False.

EDIT 2 - add the fallback. Inside def resolve_relative_date(raw) -> str | None:, find its FINAL return None. That is the LAST line of the function, immediately after the loop `for fmt in ("%m/%d", "%B %d", "%b %d"):` and its body (currently around line 603). It is NOT the early `if not t: return None` near the top. Replace ONLY that final `return None` with exactly:
    if _DATE_ORDINAL_FALLBACK:
        stripped = re.sub(r"\b(\d{1,2})(st|nd|rd|th)\b", r"\1", t)
        if stripped != t:
            return resolve_relative_date(stripped)
    return None
Notes: `t` is the already lowercased, punctuation-stripped, whitespace-collapsed string built at the top of the function. `re` is already imported at module top. The recursion terminates because the stripped string has no ordinal, so on the re-entry `stripped != t` is False and it returns None.

HARD RULES.
- Legacy-first is the whole point. Your new code runs ONLY after every existing branch failed. Do not move it earlier, do not add an else, do not touch any earlier branch, the early `if not t` return, the Chinese branches, the weekday branches, the "in N days/weeks" branches, or the explicit-date strptime loops.
- Do NOT add compound parsing, multi-cue handling, conflict/"explicit date wins" logic, or bare-day-with-month-context. Only the ordinal strip and single re-resolve.
- Do NOT change the pre-existing yearless Feb-29 -> Feb-28 line inside the yearless loop.
- Do NOT change resolve_relative_date's signature or its str | None return type.

VERIFY - run this yourself; it is exactly how you are graded:
    python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/mott/gw-temporal-check/check_gateway_datefix.py --gateway ./bland_gateway.py --golden /mnt/d_drive/repos/mott/gw-temporal-check/golden_baseline.json
It must print CHECK PASSED and exit 0. It proves: with the flag OFF the resolver is byte-identical to the original across 106 phrases (CVC untouched); with the flag ON, 96 legacy phrases are unchanged and 10 new ordinal phrases (july 28th -> 07/28/2026, august 1st -> 08/01/2026, etc.) resolve, while bare ordinals ("28th"), bad calendar dates ("february 30th"), and compounds ("tomorrow july 28th") stay None.
